text: Slack #deployments 09:12: API rollout failed because migration 0001_initial.sql was applied after the new backend started. Temporary note: retry after database migration.
Incident update 09:35: correction to earlier deployment note. The migration itself was healthy. Root cause was backend pods using an old DATABASE_URL secret after the namespace secret rotated.
Postmortem: deployment incident root cause confirmed as stale DATABASE_URL mounted in backend pods. Resolution was rollout restart after secret rotation. Migration 0001_initial.sql was not the cause.
Architecture decision: Work is the durable unit. Conversations modify Work but are not the primary durable product object.
Architecture note: Agents are durable identities. Individual executions are temporary attempts and may use different runtimes over time.
Architecture note: PostgreSQL owns durable application history. Wolverine coordinates asynchronous execution, inbox/outbox, durable messaging, and retries of delivery infrastructure.
Important correction: failed Work execution is not automatically retried. Every failure creates attention and an explicit retry is required after reconciliation.
Old brainstorm: automatically retry failed Work up to three times with exponential backoff.
GitHub integration: repositories must be explicitly enabled in Goblin before an agent can operate on them.
Slack flow: users may paste a GitHub repository URL and specify branch or push intent in natural language. A dropdown is not required in Slack or Teams.
Authentication preference: gh auth login should be exposed through the Goblin web UI for repository authorization.
Logging requirement: default log retention should be seven days. Coverage includes host VM, cluster, and individual pods.
Logging design: do not send every raw log line to the LLM. Use local filtering, anomaly detection, templates, or aggregation first to control token cost.
Candidate logging backend: VictoriaLogs stores logs efficiently and is being evaluated for the self-hosted deployment.
Candidate logging backend: Elasticsearch was considered but its memory footprint is too high for the target small VM.
UI direction: Work should be visually central. The interface should behave like a minimal project manager with tickets on the left and chat quickly accessible.
UI simplification: right-side activity should be lightweight and show external system logos in the activity thread rather than separate system tabs.
Deployment target: a single Linux VM running k3s hosts Goblin services.
Storage rule: workspace files remain on the Work PVC. Do not archive full filesystem contents into PostgreSQL.
Git checkpoints store provenance metadata, not filesystem archives. Suspending compute does not authorize deleting the Work PVC.
Memory experiment idea: SQLite FTS5 provides immediate lexical search without embeddings and is attractive as a lightweight first stage.
Memory experiment idea: local CPU-only embeddings can run asynchronously after records are immediately searchable through FTS5.
Memory pipeline proposal: incoming information goes to SQLite, is FTS5 searchable immediately, receives embedding_status pending, and a background loop later computes vectors.
Constraint: memory experiments should avoid PostgreSQL, Qdrant, Elasticsearch, Kubernetes, Docker, and external embedding APIs when evaluating the lightweight proof of concept.
Benchmark preference: compare lexical, vector, and hybrid retrieval using the same questions and corpus so results are directly comparable.
Server inventory: dedicated host has Intel i7-7700 4 cores 8 threads, 64 GB RAM, and two 512 GB NVMe drives mirrored with RAID1.
Operating system on the dedicated host is Ubuntu 26.04 LTS.
Cluster choice: k3s is preferred for the small self-hosted machine instead of a heavier Kubernetes installation.
AK3S dashboard direction: use Headlamp for Kubernetes administration and link to VictoriaMetrics and VictoriaLogs UIs rather than rebuilding those capabilities.
AK3S implementation direction: convert orchestration from Python and Ansible to a Go CLI named ak3s with embedded defaults and sparse YAML overrides.
AK3S CLI should support install, install --dry-run, apply, status, config, render, upgrade, and version commands.
AK3S normal users should not need Go, Python, Ansible, or Git installed. A minimal shell bootstrap may download the released binary.
Frontend policy: keep frontend package management and build commands in frontend/package.json using npm.
Repository orchestration policy: use a root GNU Makefile for non-frontend workflows such as build, test, checks, generation, deployment, local operations, dependencies, and formatting.
Do not move non-frontend Node tooling into frontend/package.json. Isolate required tooling such as Playwright, Prettier, TypeScript tooling, and the pinned Codex npm runtime separately.
JSON refactor rule: replace dynamic System.Text.Json DOM usage with typed POCOs when the JSON shape is known and use explicit serialization attributes.
JSON exceptions: keep dynamic JSON for CodexClient JSON-RPC envelopes, generated protocol models that explicitly allow arbitrary JSON, converters, generators, and useful raw-structure tests.
Licensing preference: commercial use is acceptable, but redistributed modified core software should preserve downstream user freedoms similar to the Linux copyleft principle.
RoslynKit goal: local semi-semantic code search via SQLite FTS5 plus BM25, without embeddings, network dependencies, or MCP.
RoslynKit token-savings target: reduce input tokens by at least twenty percent versus raw Codex while preserving correctness and relevance.
